output.headline: Accepts $75,000 from Alta Bates Summit Medical Center for the district's violence prevention program
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The action text spells the hospital as 'Alta Bates Summer Medical Center' while the title says 'Alta Bates Summit Medical Center'.
output.summary: The district is accepting a $75,000 grant from Sutter Bay Hospitals (doing business as Alta Bates Summit Medical Center) in Emeryville. The money funds the district's Violence Prevention Program, which has a dedicated program manager who develops and carries out plans to prevent youth violence for the whole student body. The grant covers January 1 through December 31, 2022, a period that began before this ratification.

vendor.name: Sutter Bay Hospitals dba Alta Bates Summit Medical Center

output.headline: Amends no-cost agreement with La Clinica de la Raza for dental care at Fremont High's health center
output.summary: This is Amendment No. 2 to a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with La Clinica de la Raza, which provides dental screening and treatment at the Tiger Health Center Clinic on the Fremont High School campus. The agreement runs July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2023 at no cost to the district, and all other terms stay the same. The text does not say what this amendment changed, and its period began before this ratification.

output.headline: Pays UC San Diego School of Medicine up to $5,000 for medical advice on student health needs

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The district is contracting with the University of California, San Diego School of Medicine, Department of Pediatrics, whose two physicians will give medical advice when district staff ask. Topics may include health protocols, students with special health care needs, what counts as medical necessity for speech, occupational and physical therapy, and standing orders for epinephrine and other stock medications. It costs up to $5,000 for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, a period that began before this ratification.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California (UC San Diego School of Medicine, Department of Pediatrics)

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $90,000 to support students whose medical needs keep them from school

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $90,000.00

output.summary: The district is contracting with an individual in Ohio to exchange information and collaborate in support of students with complex medical needs, whose ongoing treatment can make it hard to attend school. The work goes through the Special Education Department. It costs up to $90,000 for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays a speech-language pathologist up to $115,200 for students with special education plans

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $115,200.00

output.summary: The district is contracting with an individual in San Leandro to provide speech and language services as a school-based speech-language pathologist for students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). Duties include attending IEP meetings, writing progress reports, MediCal billing, assessments, case management and professional development. It costs up to $115,200 for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays STAC Physical Therapy up to $90,000 to provide physical therapy to students

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $90,000.00

output.summary: The district is contracting with STAC Physical Therapy Emeryville, Inc. to deliver direct physical therapy to students, focused on gross motor skills and access to learning in the classroom. output.headline: Accepts $2.09M California grant to support career technical education through 2023
output.summary: The district is accepting a $2,092,791 Career Technical Education Incentive Grant from the California Department of Education for its Career Technical Education Program. The money comes into the district rather than being spent on a vendor. The grant period runs July 1, 2021 through December 31, 2023.

output.headline: Accepts $4.13M state child care and development grant for early childhood program for 2022-23
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution approving Contract No. CCTR-2010 with the California Department of Education, under which the district accepts a $4,127,761 grant for the California State General Child Care and Development Program. The program is run by the district's Early Childhood Education Department. The grant covers July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Approves no-cost deal with EducationSuperHighway to help families enroll in a federal internet program
output.summary: The district is ratifying a no-cost services agreement and a data sharing agreement with EducationSuperHighway of San Francisco. The partner will help eligible district families, with priority for families without internet, enroll in a federal internet connectivity program, and the two sides will share certain non-public information tied to that effort. Both agreements run July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024, and the period began before this ratification.

output.headline: Approves three tentative agreements with the Oakland Education Association on early childhood teaching
output.summary: The Board is approving three tentative agreements with the Oakland Education Association (OEA): a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on a pilot for early childhood Teachers on Special Assignment (TSA), and two settlement agreements about teachers in itinerant roles and expanding early childhood programs to full day in 2022-23. Each runs July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. Approval depends on compliance with Government Code Section 3547.5 and state disclosure requirements. No dollar amount is stated.

output.summary: The Board is ratifying the Board President's appointment of Andrew Butler, a parent or guardian of a child enrolled in the district, to the Measures B, J, and Y Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee.
